newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-BLACK BOXES FOR GRAND PRIX CARS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BLACK BOXES FOR GRAND PRIX CARS.

text.p: Aircraft-type 'black box' accident
data recorders will be fitted to Formula One cars next season,
the International Automobile Federation (FIA) announced on
Friday.
The recorders will store information about what happens to a
car during and immediately before an accident.
The FIA believes the equipment will enhance safety and
prevent the kind of protracted investigation that followed
Ayrton Senna's fatal crash in the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix at
Imola.
"This is another major step towards improving safety," said
FIA president Max Mosley. "I am sure that the FIA/Delco
Electronics Accident Data Recorder will be regarded as a
milestone in safety research.
"We are confident this device will help us obtain an
accurate understanding of what happens during accidents. The
implications for safety are very encouraging."
The high-tech recorders are designed by U.S.-based Delco
Electronics Corporation.
"The FIA project was a complex undertaking and involved
delivering a product that could survive not only the harsh
racing environment but serious race car accidents," said David
Bastin, the company's executive director of corporate marketing.
"Our company has a significant history of developing
electronic products for motorsports that enhances both vehicle
performance and driver safety."
